channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: 2026 Booooooom Photo Awards
item.description: Booooooom's annual photography awards, run by the long-standing art and photography platform founded by Jeff Hamada. Five category winners are named across Portrait, Nature, Street, Student and Series — the last of these new for 2026 and built for cohesive bodies of work rather than single frames. Each category winner receives $1,000, a WANDRD camera bag (the PRVKE 21L for Portrait and Series, the ROGUE for Nature, Street and Student), an interview and feature on Booooooom, promotion across its social channels and a place on the awards mini-site. Three shortlisted photographers additionally receive a Manfrotto ONE Photo aluminium tripod with XPRO ball head, and sixteen participants drawn from across the whole entry pool — not only the winners — receive a hardcover photo book designed and printed by foto foto. A shortlist of twenty and a longlist of two hundred are published on the awards mini-site and across Booooooom's social channels. The jury is Katy Hundertmark, managing editor of Foam Magazine; Pat O'Rourke, founder and curator of Rental Magazine; the photographer Jennilee Marigomen; and Elena Rebecca Rivolta, editor-in-chief of PHROOM. Entry is free for a single image in one category; $25 at the early-bird rate covers up to ten images, which may span several projects, in one category; and an Awards Pass covers unlimited images across every category. Work must have been made in 2025 or 2026. The Student category is open to anyone who was enrolled in a school of any kind when the work was made, and students may enter the same work in the other categories as well. — Deadline: December 9, 2026. Fee: Free (1 image); $25 category, $50–$70 pass. Prize: 5 × $1,000 + equipment + publication feature.

item.title: Color · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed group exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe for work in which colour itself does the talking — the next call in the gallery's rolling monthly programme, following Darkness and Black and White on the same board. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, a fine art photographer whose work has been exhibited and published internationally; 26 images are selected for the gallery walls. The gallery covers the whole cost of presentation — one exhibition-quality print on Luster paper, custom framing in the gallery's signature 24×24 inch black museum-quality frames, and matting from its collection of precut white mats, resized by the gallery's team without cropping the original composition. Artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG between 500KB and 5MB with the longest side at 4,500 pixels. The exhibition runs March 5 to 26 with an opening reception on March 5; the year is not printed on the page, but March 5 2027 is the first Friday of that month, which is the gallery's own stated scheduling convention, and the January 28 2027 deadline with its two-week notification window leaves no room for a 2026 show. After the show the physical print is archived in the gallery's flat files, photographers retain all rights to their images, and any sale splits 50/50 between gallery and photographer. Acceptance is emailed within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution files are due within two days of that email. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Entry is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10, non-refundable. — Deadline: January 28, 2027. Fee: $40/5 images, $45/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Kranj Foto Fest Open Call for Exhibitions 2027
item.description: The exhibition open call for the seventh edition of Kranj Foto Fest, a Slovenian festival of contemporary photography founded in 2021 and run by the non-profit Zavod Photo Dialogue. Up to thirteen projects are selected. Twelve of them enter group exhibitions with the festival covering the full production cost of the work — printing and installation — plus three nights' accommodation during opening week, 26–29 August 2027. From those, one grand prize winner receives a solo exhibition with production costs covered, a €1,000 cash prize and up to €400 in travel support to attend the festival. There is no thematic or technical restriction, but the photographs must form a coherent story, series or project. Applicants may be photographers, visual artists or visual storytellers working individually, in duos or as collectives, from anywhere in the world, and the terms set a floor of 18 years. Each project is 10 to 20 JPG images with a minimum of 1,500 pixels on the longest edge, submitted at a resolution suitable for printing, with a project description of up to 2,500 characters and a bio of up to 1,500; text may be in Slovene or English, and English is recommended. Up to two projects may be entered, at €12 for one and €16 for both. Artists who have exhibited at the festival before may reapply only with a different project; festival staff, sponsors, jury members and their relatives may not apply. The jury is Maryam Wahid of Tasweer Photo Biennale, Amin Yousefi of Photoworks and Photography+, Edda Fahrenhorst of horizonte zingst and Yeast Photo Festival, Peter Rauch of the University of Ljubljana's Academy of Fine Arts and Design, and festival founding director Fernanda Prado Verčič. Judging takes place in January 2027 and results are emailed in February. The 2027 festival runs 26 August to 26 September in Kranj. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: €12 (€16 for two projects). Prize: Solo exhibition + €1,000 + €400 travel.

item.title: Arty Rat Magazine Open Call — December 2026
item.description: Arty Rat is an independent art journal run from Vienna by curator Oleksandr Dyvnich, showcasing contemporary visual art, illustration and “bold creative voices from around the world”; the open call page addresses itself to “artists and photographers”. This is the next rolling cycle after the 1 November one, at the same standing call page. Submission is free, open worldwide to applicants 18 or older, and up to six works may be entered as JPG or PNG — either through the form on the call page, or by pasting a Google Drive or Dropbox link into it, or by emailing the files to the journal. Selected artists receive a free digital copy of the magazine as a PDF, photographs of their printed magazine pages and a feature on the journal's Instagram; two selected artists have their work on the magazine covers, and one selected artist takes part free of charge in a group exhibition at The Names Gallery in Vienna — a show the call page still dates only as “the end of August” with no year. A participation fee applies only if the work is selected, and the organiser lists the options openly: €35 for publication in the magazine, €65 for publication plus an artist's page on the website with biography, statement and photographs of works, €100 for a curatorial review covering magazine and website, and €100 for the Vienna exhibition. The fee is non-refundable. The most recent issue, Issue 5, was published in September 2026. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free (€35–€100 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: BINGO February 2027 — Cheek to Cheek · Candela Photographic Arts
item.description: The second run of Candela's “give two, get one” small-print open call, and the first with a theme. Candela Photographic Arts — the Richmond, Virginia gallery and independent photobook publisher that became a 501(c)(3) in 2026 after fifteen years as Candela Books + Gallery — asks for “interpretations of touch and fresh takes on the photographic tradition of the nude – particularly, the beloved bottom”. Cheek to Cheek “explores intimacy through touch, gesture and form”: hugs, kisses, caresses, the spaces between, or a favourite derrière, with unconventional, experimental and playful readings of every form of love explicitly welcome. The gallery adds its own disclaimer — keep the work “thoughtful, playful, and/or conceptual”, because Candela “isn't interested in nude imagery that feels exploitative or needlessly vulgar”. Fourteen small photographic works are selected and hang from 8 January to 13 February 2027, alongside Candela's January/February solo exhibitions, before a ticketed Valentine's bingo fundraiser on 13 February at which every framed print on view goes home with a winner. Selected artists send two unframed editions of their image: the first is an in-kind donation that Candela frames and mats at its own cost and gives away on Bingo Day, the second enters a randomised swap that mails another participant's print back to the artist, postage covered by the gallery. Submission is free — “there is no fee to submit to the Bingo show” — and opened on 3 November 2026. Up to three photographic prints may be entered; each must exist in at least two editions (variant editions accepted) and measure no more than 12 inches on the longest side. Submissions take 1–3 JPEGs, the artist's contact details, each work's title, year, medium, dimensions and edition information, and a short statement or bio. Accepted artists are announced on 1 December 2026 and must ship both prints to the gallery by 15 December. Candela encourages alternative processes, tiny prints, variant editions, and work from “side quests, one-off projects, proofs, or works-in-progress” as readily as finished bodies of work — and is candid that the exhibition “is philanthropic and community-focused in nature and may not be a great fit for artists looking for big sales opportunities”. The gallery names no juror. Artists after the gallery's flagship juried show are pointed at UnBound16!, whose own open call runs 5 January to 12 February 2027. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + print swap.

item.title: Prix Roger Pic 2027 · LaScam
item.description: LaScam — the Société civile des auteurs multimédia, the French authors' society for multimedia work — has run the Prix Roger Pic since 1993, named for the humanist photographer, director and copyright campaigner who instigated it, and awards it each year to the author of a photographic portfolio that documents the real and questions the human with singularity. This is the 35th edition, run in partnership with Fisheye magazine. The award is €4,000, and with it comes €1,240 (gross, or excluding tax) in droits de monstration — an exhibition fee paid to the winner for showing the awarded portfolio in LaScam's own gallery in Paris, where Vincent Gouriou's Les ombres claires, the 2026 winner, hangs from 5 October 2026 to 19 February 2027. LaScam states the prize is meant for photographers whose talent has not yet had the recognition it deserves, and the roll of laureates is the best argument for entering: Vincent Gouriou (2026), Véronique de Viguerie (2025), Corentin Fohlen (2024), Mário Macilau (2023), Baudouin Mouanda (2022), Alexis Vettoretti (2021), Sandra Reinflet (2020), Tomas van Houtryve and Denis Dailleux (2019), Laura El-Tantawy (2018), Michael Ackerman (2009), Christian Lutz (2011) and Martin Kollar (2005). Entry is free and there is no membership requirement — work is read from photographers who do not belong to LaScam — but the call is for professional photographers over 18, of French or any other nationality. The portfolio must be unpublished and must not have won any award (contest, festival, book, slideshow) before the date of registration; one portfolio per author per year, and a different one each year; only complete bodies of work are considered, never unfinished projects. Note the language condition, which is easy to miss and decides whether you can apply: accompanying texts must be written or translated into French. The online file is a portfolio of 20 photographs (JPG, 1–5 MB each, at least 2000 pixels on the long side, with IPTC title, description and photographer's name), a title and caption of up to 300 characters for each photograph, a 900-character summary plus a presentation and letter of intent (PDF, two A4 portrait pages maximum), and a biography of the author and any co-authors (same format). Two stages follow: the authors of LaScam's commission des images fixes draw up a pre-selection of ten portfolios, then a jury renewed every year — commission members, the president of the LaScam-Vélasquez association, and outside figures from photography, where possible including a previous laureate — picks the winner from those ten, with registrations processed December to February and the pre-selection and jury sitting March to April. Two conditions sit in the regulations rather than the call text, and registering online is what accepts them: photographs entirely generated by AI are not accepted, and every candidate grants LaScam free use of up to two of their photographs to promote the prize, worldwide for a year and tacitly renewed unless cancelled two months before the year ends. The deposit page runs 4–30 November 2026 and opens at 08:00 Paris time on the first day. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €4,000 + €1,240 exhibition rights + Exhibition.

item.title: Artistic Calendar 2027 · iTravelPoetry
item.description: iTravelPoetry — a Greek publisher and cultural venue in Chalandri, in the Athens suburbs, whose photography programme runs the Beyond Borders open call and its own festival — is assembling the Artistic Calendar 2027 (Καλλιτεχνικό Ημερολόγιο 2027), a collective edition that turns a year of days into a printed anthology of reader and contributor work. Four entry categories are named and photography is one of them: a poem of up to 30 lines, a text or short story of up to 500 words, a painting or other visual work, or a photograph. The theme is free. Each creator may enter one or two works — €13 for one, €20 for two, plus shipping, and each option includes one copy of the finished book; extra copies are €10 each. Work in another art form, or work over the line or word limit, is priced separately on request. Be clear about what the fee buys: the call names no jury and describes no selection stage for the four listed categories, and its own words are an invitation to participate and a “confirmation of your participation”, so the €13 buys a place in the edition rather than a shot at one — the organiser's framing is that creators carry none of the production cost, and with a €10 copy included the real entry cost is a few euros plus postage. The edition is a printed A5 book, black-and-white throughout (worth weighing if you work in colour), carries an ISBN and a BookPoint registration, and is launched at the publisher's own cultural space at Irakleiou 6, Chalandri. Under Greek copyright law 2121/1993 the copyright stays with the creator and the exploitation rights sit with the publisher, but the works are explicitly not bound editorially to iTravelPoetry, so you may use the same work in other editions of your own or in other collections. Entry is through the form on the call page, which takes the finished file (JPG, PNG, DOC, DOCX or PDF) and asks for a postal address for the copy; payment is by bank transfer to an account sent with the confirmation of your participation, with any bank charges on the sender. The form also makes you pick one of four promotion options before it will submit — a photo and CV added (€10 + VAT), a written interview on the publisher's site (€20 + VAT), a professional video feature (€200 + VAT), or “no promotion, calendar entry only” — and that last one is free, so none of it belongs to the entry price. The call is published only in Greek and its form asks for your name in Greek characters, so a non-Greek-speaking photographer should expect to write to the publisher before entering. Submit the final file: the organiser states that no changes are accepted after submission. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: €13 (1 work) / €20 (2 works) + postage. Prize: Publication + contributor copy.

item.title: Snow Much to See 2026
item.description:
Snow Much to See is an international photography contest devoted to snow, ice and cold, now in its second edition. It is run by the photographer Giandra De Castro and is part of the programme of Images & Neige, a festival founded in Cluses, in the Haute-Savoie Alps, by the photographer Frédéric Boiteux, which describes itself as the only photography festival in Europe entirely devoted to that theme. The festival's 17th edition runs from 22 to 24 January 2027. Every photograph must have an identifiable link with snow, ice or cold.
Entries compete in 11 categories, each open to single images and to series of 3 to 20 photographs: snowy or icy landscapes; scenes of winter life; urban environments shaped by cold or snow; winter sports and leisure; wildlife and plants in cold environments; the human, social or environmental consequences of cold; poetry and reverie; minimalism, graphics and abstraction; macro and close-up; smartphone; and drone. The last three are defined by technique and accept any subject. An entrant may submit up to 60 single images and several series, and the same photograph can be entered both ways, in which case it is judged and charged twice.
Seven winners are exhibited at the festival, with production paid for by the organisers. Four series winners each have three photographs chosen by the jury, printed in a 40 × 60 format with pigment inks on Hahnemühle paper and framed in wooden box frames. Three single-image winners, a first, second and third prize, are printed in 30 × 45. The prints stay with the organisers. Each category also awards one single-image prize and one series prize. No prize carries cash. Winners, category winners and jury favourites appear in the exhibition catalogue with the jury's written analysis.
Free photographs exist in only two categories, Sport and Urban. In each, the first single image and the first two photographs of a series kept in that category are free, so two single images can be entered at no cost. A series needs at least three photographs, so a series always costs something. Paid photographs from both formats are added together and charged once: €5 for up to 3, €10 for up to 10, €15 for up to 20, and €2 for each one beyond 20. From €5, the entrant receives a PDF of the catalogue with every photograph commented. From €25, which is 25 paid photographs — the organiser advertises this tier as "31 photos", counting the 6 free ones — the entry also gets a one-page written review, sent on 11 January 2027. Fees are not refunded unless the contest is cancelled.
Files are JPEGs of at least 2,000 pixels on the long side, with no watermark, signature or frame, and judging is anonymous. Usual editing is allowed, including panoramas, exposure blending and focus stacking from the entrant's own shots. Photomontages and images generated or altered by artificial intelligence are not accepted, and the original file may be requested. The jury is Giandra De Castro (president), Frédéric Boiteux and three people from the City of Cluses, which hosts the exhibition: Françoise Guillen, Priyam Nursimhulu and Manon Canale. Entrants keep their copyright. For selected photographs only, the organisers and the City of Cluses receive a free, non-exclusive five-year permission covering the results, the exhibition, the catalogue and promotion.
The contest is open to amateur, semi-professional and professional photographers of any nationality aged 18 or over. Entries close on 30 November 2026 at 23:59 Paris time, and results are announced on 21 December 2026. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free (2 photos); €5 / €10 / €15 for 3 / 10 / 20 paid photos, +€2 each after. Prize: Exhibition at Images & Neige, Cluses (7 winners, production covered) + 22 category prizes.

item.title: Beyond Borders — International Photography Exhibition · iTravelPoetry
item.description: A three-city touring photography exhibition from iTravelPoetry, an independent Greek cultural organisation that runs a cultural venue in Chalandri, Athens, alongside a poetry competition, a film festival and publications. Its first photography festival closed with the group show "Within the Frame" at that venue in October 2026. Beyond Borders asks photographers to work with borders of any kind — geographical, cultural, social, emotional or entirely personal — or to challenge the idea of a border altogether; every genre and technique is welcome, from documentary and street to conceptual and experimental. Open to photographers aged 18 and over of any nationality, experience or background, with up to three images per applicant submitted by email as JPGs with titles. Read the cost carefully before applying: applying is free, but a €150 participation fee is charged to photographers whose work is selected and who then confirm their place, covering all three cities with no per-city extra. Selected photographs are shown in Athens, Paris and Rome, but the organisers state that exhibition dates and venue details will only be announced after submissions close, and no jury, prize or sales terms are published. Submissions run 17 October to 30 November 2026. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free (€150 if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: KG+ 2027 Open Call · KYOTOGRAPHIE
item.description: KG+ is the satellite programme of the KYOTOGRAPHIE International Photography Festival, launched in 2013 to discover and support emerging artists and curators; 2027 is its fifteenth edition. Applicants propose a solo or group exhibition of photography — or of work incorporating photographic elements, including moving image and installation — to be staged at a venue in Kyoto City during the festival, 17 April to 16 May 2027. Applications are open regardless of age, profession, nationality or experience, but applicants must secure their own venue before applying and submit a signed venue usage permission form; the exhibition must be open to the public for at least nine days of the festival period, at least one of them a weekend or Japanese national holiday. Selected exhibitions enter the official KG+ programme in one of two categories (KG+ PICK UP or KG+), are published on the festival website and map, receive free promotional signage, and are eligible for discounted KYOTOGRAPHIE masterclasses and portfolio reviews, as well as the KG+ Discovery Award. The application fee is JPY 18,000, non-refundable, and includes one KYOTOGRAPHIE 2027 Passport. Note that participants bear all exhibition costs themselves — venue rental, printing, framing, transport, installation and deinstallation. Applications close 31 December 2026 at 23:59 JST; applicants are notified by late January 2027, and those who apply by 30 November 2026 hear by the end of 2026. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: ¥18,000 (incl. festival passport). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Weir Farm Artist-in-Residence Program
item.description:
A one-month residency on the 68-acre Weir Farm National Historical Park in Wilton, Connecticut, continuing "the creative legacy of Julian Alden Weir by supporting contemporary artists whose work advances artistic dialogue and innovation." Over 250 artists have taken part; the park's enabling legislation "underscores the importance of maintaining an active artistic presence," and the programme is framed as fostering "contemporary visual art practices that engage with and interpret the world in creative, experimental, and thought-provoking ways." One artist is in residence at a time, for four weeks between May and October 2027.
Photography is named explicitly: applicants "may apply in any of the following visual art media: Painting, Photography, Printmaking, Sculpture, Fiber Art, Mixed Media," and the park "encourages applications from artists representing a wide range of perspectives and media." Housing and studio space are provided — a fully furnished historic residence in the middle of the park, and the AIR Studio a few steps away, built in 2010 on the footprint of the former garage and awarded the NPS Certificate of Honor. Artists receive a $400 stipend, $200 at the start and $200 after the residency on completion of the requirements. Artists supply their own food, personal items and art supplies and provide their own transportation to and from the park, and the park warns the site "is very quiet and dark at night."
On accessibility: the programme "welcomes artists of all physical capabilities"; the art studio and restroom are wheelchair accessible, the historic cottage is not, and artists are not required to stay in the cottage, though off-site accommodation is at their own expense.
Open to US citizens and permanent residents aged 25 or over who are graduate students, emerging or professional artists, applying as individuals — couples and collectives are not considered. Anyone who held a residency between 2017 and 2026 is ineligible for the 2027 cohort. Residents must commit to the full four weeks, attend a welcome event, present a public Open Studio on the last Saturday of the residency, send 3–5 images mid-residency for social media, and take part in a recorded Zoom interview. Outdoor installations, open flame, kilns, toxic or hazardous materials, collecting natural materials on federal land and selling work on site are all prohibited.
A three-member jury drawn from academia, museums, galleries, professional artists and former residents weighs artistic merit, a well-defined and realistic project proposal, the answer to the "Why Weir Farm" question, and the artist's ability to commit. All applicants are notified by mid-March 2027. The programme is supported by the Friends of Weir Farm NHP, with a 2027 grant from the Connecticut company Tauck. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: $35. Prize: $400 stipend + Residency (1 month).

item.title: Elemental · Artspiration Frederick
item.description:
"Earth. Water. Air. Fire." A juried exhibition at Artspiration Frederick "where artists explore these powerful forces of nature and the ways they intersect with materiality, imagination, and the human experience." Artists are encouraged to interpret the elements "literally, symbolically, or abstractly, exploring themes of transformation, resilience, movement, balance, and change", and — working across all mediums — to consider "not only the elements themselves, but also the physical properties of their materials and the processes through which their work takes shape." The gallery says it welcomes "innovative and thought-provoking interpretations that reveal the extraordinary possibilities found within nature's most fundamental forces."
All media are accepted and photography is named among them. Up to three exhibition-ready works may be submitted and up to three may be selected, each needing a 300 dpi image for jurying; 2D work must be framed with a wire for hanging (no sawtooth hangers). Open to visual artists 18 and over residing in the continental US. The show runs 2–25 April 2027 at 915 Toll House Ave in Frederick, with an opening reception on 10 April, free and open to the public. Accepted work is dropped off 28–30 March or shipped to arrive by 30 March at the artist's cost, with a return label included, and retrieved by 10 May.
All work must be for sale and the gallery retains 40% of the sale price, the artist 60%. Prices are locked at entry — the gallery will not accept price changes once a piece has been submitted.
The juror is Lisa Sheirer, who has a BFA in painting and printmaking from West Virginia University and an MFA in sculpture from Notre Dame, works in "pixels, clay, ink, paint, wood, and sound", and is an artist in residence at the Ausherman Y Arts Center in downtown Frederick. Her public work includes a ceramic mural at Baltimore-Washington International Airport for the Maryland Department of Transportation and a glass mural at UPMC Western Maryland Hospital; she self-published the artist book "WaterShed" in 2023 with an NEA/Frederick Arts Council grant and holds the Jean Royer Kohr Memorial Lectureship. — Deadline: March 12, 2027. Fee: $35 ($25 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SO THEY SAY — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
item.description:
A public art exhibition on bus shelter ad space in Miami, opening 30 December 2026 and curated by Katelyn Kopenhaver. The brief turns the medium on itself: "Advertising follows us everywhere. From our phones to the streets, it appears on screens floating in the ocean or hovering above our heads. We are constantly being sold something: a product, a belief, an emotion, or an idea of who we should aspire to be. These messages seep into our subconscious, shaping our perceptions and sense of identity, often without question or consent."
SaveArtSpace asks for work "specifically conceived for the bus shelter, rather than treating it as an alternative gallery wall" — "operating within the very infrastructure it seeks to examine". Through humour and/or critical inquiry, artists are encouraged to engage with the mechanics of advertising, "playing with expectations and turning a space designed to persuade us into one that questions what we're being told."
Open to "artists of all ages and talents". Up to 10 JPEGs, each a maximum of 2 MB; selected artists are asked for high-resolution files afterwards. Selected artists are announced after 7 December 2026 and the work goes up on Miami bus shelter ad space from 30 December for at least one month. Fees are framed as tax-deductible donations that buy the ad space itself. The organiser’s FAQ adds that anyone who cannot afford the donation may submit their work by email instead, with the name of the open call as the subject.
The curator, Katelyn Kopenhaver (b. 1992), took a BFA in Photography from the School of Visual Arts and works across public intervention, performance, text and lens-based media; she is a studio resident at Bakehouse Art Complex in Miami, a NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellow (2021) and a Miami Individual Artist Grant recipient (2024 and 2026), and appeared in Der Greif Issue 18 curated by Hank Willis Thomas. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images) + $10 each additional ($36.92–$108.45 at checkout). Prize: Bus shelter exhibition in Miami.

item.title: Persistence of Memory · A Photographer's Place
item.description:
A monthly juried show in Gallery X at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, built on the question "If the past is never entirely gone, what remains?" The gallery invites photographic artists to submit work for an exhibition "examining the complex and often elusive relationship between memory, time, and perception", noting that while "a photograph can preserve a fleeting moment, but memory is far less predictable. It distorts, reconstructs, conceals, and reveals."
The call seeks "images that consider what remains after the moment has passed" — the imprint of a person, the familiarity of a place, the weight of history, the passage of time, or the fragments of an experience that refuse to fade. Interpretations that are personal, historical, psychological, conceptual, poetic or experimental are all encouraged, as is work exploring remembrance and forgetting, nostalgia and displacement, identity and transformation, or "the blurred boundaries between what is real and what is remembered". Selection weighs relevance to the theme, technical quality and originality, and artistic vision and storytelling.
Selected work hangs in Gallery X at the front of the space from 4 December 2026 to 2 January 2027, with an opening reception on 4 December, and is then presented on the gallery's website to be viewed year-round. Up to 5 JPEGs, colour or black and white, minimum 3000 pixels on the longest side; work must be delivered to the gallery by 2 December. Accepted artists may optionally have their work printed by the gallery on its Canon imagePROGRAF PRO-1100. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 5 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibit Your Work — Exhibition Proposals · Photosynthesis NZ
item.description:
Photosynthesis, the volunteer-run photography gallery, darkroom and studio on Battersea Street in Sydenham, Ōtautahi Christchurch, takes exhibition proposals all year through an expression-of-interest form. Its exhibitions run in sponsored seasons of ten weeks at no cost to the exhibitors, with one or two shows on at a time, each for two or three weeks. Proposals are welcome from emerging, mid-career and established artists, collectives, curators and community groups, for photography in the broadest sense: anything made using light.
The expression of interest covers the proposed show's content, representative images, duration and dates, information about the artist and what is needed from the gallery's volunteers. A curation panel of community peers reviews it and recommends accepting, revising or declining the show, and a selected artist receives a letter of acceptance. Exhibitors install the show, hold an opening on its first Wednesday, staff the gallery on run days and pack out, with volunteer help on request, and are encouraged to run workshops, talks or demonstrations. The large wall is 13.8 m long with a 2.4 m display height; the smaller area has 9 m of wall with optional suspended panels. Exhibiting artists can print at the gallery's rentable digital workspace.
The page names two 2026 seasons, from 29 June and from 28 September, both already under way; no later season is published yet. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: MOP: Black Tie · Valkarie Gallery
item.description: Valkarie Gallery's entry in Denver's Month of Photography 2027: a juried show of classic black-and-white photography in Lakewood, Colorado. The gallery asks for "traditional, sleek, and elegant black-and-white photography that embraces the power of light, shadow, and form" — from high-contrast street portraits and cinematic architectural geometries to minimalist landscapes and editorial fashion — and says it is looking for "technical mastery, deliberate composition, and a refined aesthetic that honors the rich heritage of silver-halide and classic archival black-and-white printing", photographs that "command attention without the noise of color". Eligible mediums are named: traditional silver gelatin prints, darkroom processes, digital black-and-white and archival monochrome inkjet prints. The jurors are Valkarie residents and Denver photographers Robert Newman and McCory James. Entry is $20 for up to three original 2D works, open to anyone who lives or works in Colorado; no AI art is accepted, no digital enhancement is allowed, and work may not exceed 36 × 36 inches. Artists are notified by Friday 19 February 2027, accepted work is dropped off at the gallery between 20 and 28 February, and the exhibition runs 4 to 28 March 2027 with an opening reception on Saturday 6 March, 5–8.30pm. Work must be delivered protected and labelled with the artist's name, phone number, price and title; the gallery takes a 30% commission on sales, prices cannot be changed after acceptance, sold work stays on the wall until the show closes, and payment reaches the artist within a month of closing. Valkarie, open since November 2013, describes itself as an artist collective; the gallery is at 445 S Saulsbury Street and is the winner of Lakewood's Community 2026 Platinum Award for best in art dealers and arts & crafts. — Deadline: February 14, 2027. Fee: $20 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Secrets · Falkirk Cultural Center
item.description: Juried winter show at the Falkirk Cultural Center, a city-run gallery in a Queen Anne mansion in San Rafael, on the theme of secrets. The centre's framing: "Secrets is an invitation to explore the many layers of what is hidden and what is revealed. Secrets can be personal or collective, real or imagined, inherited or invented. What might be concealed behind a face, beneath a landscape, inside an object, or between the lines of a story. What happens when something hidden comes into the light? Consider what you choose to reveal, what you choose to obscure and what you leave for the viewer to uncover." Open to artists residing in the nine counties of the San Francisco Bay Area — Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano and Sonoma — who may submit up to three separate original works not previously shown at Falkirk; all media are eligible except jewellery, AI-created images and videography. One caution before you pay: the prospectus contradicts itself on how old the work may be, saying “completed in the past two years” in its opportunity summary and “past five years” in its general information, and two years is the window Falkirk's previous call used — ask the gallery before entering anything older than that. One digital image per work. The selection juror and curator is Susan Press, who studied printmaking and ceramics at the San Francisco Art Institute and has curated and juried shows in San Rafael for Artworks Downtown, the Marin Society of Artists and Falkirk itself; the awards juror is Bree Woodward, a Bay Area figurative sculptor, creative director and arts educator. Awards of $100, $75 and $50 are presented at the opening reception on Friday 8 January 2027, 5–7.30pm, during San Rafael's Art Walk, with the ceremony around 6.30pm; the exhibition runs 8 January to 19 February 2027. Entry is $40 for the first work and $7.50 each for a second and third; diptychs and triptychs count as one piece. Notifications go out by Friday 11 December 2026, with a separate email for each work. Accepted work must be hand delivered to the gallery at 1408 Mission Avenue on Monday 4 January 2027 between 10am and 2pm — shipping is not accepted — must be ready to hang with wire on D-rings or mirror hangers, and the City of San Rafael retains a 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: $40, $7.50 each additional. Prize: $100 / $75 / $50.

item.title: 2027 Artworks Northwest Biennial · Umpqua Valley Arts
item.description: Umpqua Valley Arts' regional biennial: a juried and curated showcase of contemporary work by artists living in the Pacific Northwest, with space for more than 100 works. The organisers invite artists at all stages of their careers — established, mid-career and emerging — residing in Oregon, Washington, Idaho, Northern California, Alaska, British Columbia, Western Montana or Western Wyoming. All themes, genres and media are eligible except video; fine art prints including c-prints and digital prints are explicitly eligible but must be signed, numbered and in a limited edition of 125 or fewer, and no reproductions of original artworks are accepted. Work must have been made in the last three years, not shown at UVA before, and must stay within 60 inches on its longest side, fit through a standard three-foot door and weigh under 50 lbs. Each artist may enter up to three works; on CaFE every image counts as a submission, so the organisers recommend one image per piece to leave room for more works. Selection is by a single invited curator who lives and works in the region — the list of past curators runs through Grace Kook-Anderson, Steven Hayes, Marie Watt, Andries Fourie, Scott Malbaurn, Arvie Smith and Charlene Liu — and the 2027 curator is the Portland artist Brenda Mallory, a citizen of the Cherokee Nation whose sculptures sew reclaimed materials together with industrial hardware to explore dominion, disruption and repair, and who has held Joan Mitchell, Hallie Ford and Bonnie Bronson Fellowships. Accepted works are then juried again for cash awards: $500 first place, $250 second, $150 third and the $100 J. Lynn Peterson Award. Entry is $35 and UVA members get 10% off with a coupon code from the exhibitions coordinator. Artists are notified no later than 5 May 2027, work is delivered on 7 June, and the exhibition runs 11 June to 21 August 2027 in Roseburg, Oregon. — Deadline: March 26, 2027. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: $500 / $250 / $150 + $100 J. Lynn Peterson Award.

item.title: Artist Occupied 2027/2028 Residencies · Firehouse Art Center
item.description: The Firehouse Art Center in Longmont, Colorado runs two Artist Occupied residencies a year, each working in the public South Gallery before a culminating solo exhibition in the Main Gallery, with the option to guest curate the accompanying South Gallery show. One application covers both cycles: the summer residency runs 1 July to 11 September 2027 with its exhibition opening 11 September 2027, and the winter residency runs 1 November 2027 to 6 February 2028 with its exhibition opening 11 February 2028. The centre frames the programme as professional development for emerging and experienced visual artists, connecting visitors to working artist environments and processes. The studio is 350 sq ft with natural light and tall ceilings, a full sink, limited basement storage, wi-fi, 24-hour building access and use of the kiln. Residents are asked to work in the space at least ten hours a week — five hours on each of two days during open gallery hours, Wednesday to Sunday 12–5pm — so that the public can watch the work happen, and to schedule at least three public events such as a workshop or artist talk, with workshop fees paid to the artist. One piece of original work must be donated to the Firehouse for its annual Gala auction. A materials budget may be submitted with the application; the stipend is project-specific and set by the Exhibits Committee. Applying is free: complete the centre's form and email a PDF with a site-specific proposal for the work to be made during the residency, a statement of why you want the residency, an artist statement, an account of how your work or process will engage the community during studio time, 8–10 images of recent work, a materials budget if applicable, an artist resume, three references and contact details. Selection weighs the merit of past work, readiness to benefit from the residency, a demonstrable interest in interactive, participatory or socially engaged practice, and the potential to develop an innovative practice in public. Applicants must currently live and work in Boulder County or the surrounding area and be able to commute to the centre for the whole residency period. Short-listing is announced 15 February 2027, interviews are the week of 27 February 2027, and the final selection is announced 6 March 2027. Past residents include Heather Kegel, Kaitlyn Tucek, Kenzie Sitterud, Jessica Forrestal and Mollie Jackson. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + solo exhibition + project stipend.

item.title: Architecture Interpreted · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: International juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on architecture as a subject of perception rather than a record of buildings. The gallery's framing: the built environment is everywhere, from monumental icons to ordinary spaces, but how we see and interpret it transforms structure into art — architecture is not only construction but form, light, rhythm and cultural memory. Praxis invites work that moves beyond simple documentation, revealing design, geometry, scale, atmosphere and the dialogue between structure and space; interiors, exteriors, urban or rural settings, historical sites and contemporary forms are all admissible so long as the focus is how architecture is visually or conceptually realised. All lens-based submissions are welcome. The juror is Adam Reynolds, an architecture and design photographer based in Minneapolis whose work connects the built environment to political conflict, and who has published Architecture of an Existential Threat (2017), on Israeli bomb shelters, and COUNTDOWN (2022), co-authored with Jeanne Michna-Bales, on America's Cold War nuclear infrastructure. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (19 December 2026 – 9 January 2027), featured on the gallery's online exhibition page and permanently archived there. Awards are a Juror's Choice (free entry into three future juried calls of the artist's choice), a Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery. Entrants must be 18 or older, and images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission from the gallery. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames and retains a 50% commission on any print sales. Notification is 30 November 2026. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Boundaries 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: New-theme international photography exhibition at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography, running 1 to 25 April 2027. "Boundaries are all around us, physical limitations or social agreements, they can keep us safe or restrict us. You can stay within these boundaries or you can break free of them" — the gallery wants to see how photographers interpret the theme, "either literal or in a more metaphorical sense", and says you can be as experimental as you wish. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (sRGB, 300ppi, 3000 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer — Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox — to the gallery's submissions address; attachments are discouraged because they compress the files, and all images should be sent together. Selected work is printed and displayed in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the gallery's website, and included in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants also receive a digital certificate of participation before the exhibition opens, have their installed work photographed and filmed for the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers who are selected pay a £50 participation fee covering printing and installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image, and a discount is available to anyone selected for both April exhibitions. Acceptance notification is by 25 November 2026 and the payment deadline for selected photographers is 9 December 2026. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Monochrome 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Open-themed black-and-white photography exhibition at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography, running 1 to 25 April 2027. The gallery calls it "the return of one of our most popular exhibitions" and sets no subject brief: "With Monochrome you can take out other distractions and really focus on the light, the shadow and the subject within the image. Any subject matter will be considered as long as the image is monochrome, whether that be black and white photography, cyanotypes, or even sepia; all will be considered." Submit up to 8 JPEGs (sRGB, 300ppi, 3000 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer — Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox — to the gallery's submissions address; attachments are discouraged because they compress the files, and all images should be sent together. Selected work is printed and displayed in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the gallery's website, and included in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants also receive a digital certificate of participation before the exhibition opens, have their installed work photographed and filmed for the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers who are selected pay a £50 participation fee covering printing and installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image, and a discount is available to anyone selected for both April exhibitions. Acceptance notification is by 25 November 2026 and the payment deadline for selected photographers is 9 December 2026. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Coming Together · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: End-of-year open call from Fotografiska Emerging on community and shared celebration. "As the year draws to a close, we invite artists to share images that explore community and shared celebration. From gatherings around a family table to moments of belonging within a chosen community, we want to see the different ways people come together around the world. We welcome unexpected interpretations alongside familiar scenes." The organiser's question to applicants is "Where do you find togetherness, and what does it look like through your lens?" Five artists are each selected, and each receives €300 in prize money, a feature on the Fotografiska Emerging platform, a feature on Instagram through @fotografiska and @fotografiska.emerging, and a mention in the Emerging newsletter. Entry is free: submit one image per submission, up to five images in total, as JPG or PNG at a minimum width of 1,600–2,000 pixels and no more than 5 MB, with an English caption (or an English translation) of up to 1,000 characters beginning with a sentence introducing yourself. AI-generated images are not accepted. A jury of the Fotografiska Emerging team and a Fotografiska curator selects the winning images on artistic and creative merit and relevance to the theme. The call period runs from 2 November 2026 at 10:00 CET to 3 December 2026 at 10:00 CET, and the selected artists are featured individually between 21 and 27 December 2026. Open to anyone aged 18 or over; Fotografiska group employees and their relatives are excluded. — Deadline: December 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €300 × 5 + platform and Instagram feature.

item.title: DPG Masters Underwater Imaging Competition 2026 · DivePhotoGuide
item.description: DivePhotoGuide's flagship underwater imaging competition, which the organisers describe as "a long-established and widely respected contest that celebrates the splendor of the oceans and the challenging art of underwater photography and video" and call on "underwater shooters of all levels to compete in what has become the 'World Championship' of international underwater imagery events." Prizes are worth more than $90,000 in total and include dive trips with resorts and liveaboards and top underwater imaging and dive gear; entrants compete across 11 categories — Unrestricted, Traditional, Macro, Wide Angle, Conservation, Blackwater, Smartphone, Portfolio (six images), Cold Water and Compact Camera for stills, plus Short Film for video (five minutes or less, at least half shot underwater) — and the photographer or filmmaker behind the top entry among the category winners is crowned DPG Grand Master 2026, taking the top trip prize as well as the top equipment prizes. Selected finalists are also offered a "mentor prize": an hour-long one-to-one video portfolio review with one of the judges. The jury is chaired by Nicolas Remy and includes National Geographic contributing photographer David Doubilet, Jennifer Hayes, Henley Spiers, Ipah Uid Lynn and Renee Capozzola. Entry is $10 per image or video, and 15% of entry proceeds are donated to marine conservation. Work that has already won a prize, commendation or award in any major photo or video contest before 30 September 2026 may not be entered, and entrants under 18 need a parent or guardian's consent. Submissions close Friday 8 January 2027 at 11:59PM PST; entries are shortlisted 11–15 January, judged 16–28 January, finalists' RAW files are examined, awards are decided 1–3 February, and winners are announced in late February 2027 on UnderwaterCompetition.com and published by supporting media partners worldwide. — Deadline: January 8, 2027. Fee: $10 per image or video. Prize: $90,000 prize pool (dive trips and imaging gear).

item.title: The Alchemy of Healing 2027 · Art League of New Britain
item.description: Juried group exhibition at the Art League of New Britain's Low + Lacey Galleries, 9 January – 14 February 2027, "exploring the transformative power of pain, adversity, grief, illness, trauma, and lived experience." The exhibition asks one question — "What can we create from what has hurt us?" — and explicitly refuses the tidy version of the answer: "Healing is often presented as a moment when the pain is gone and everything is made whole again. The Alchemy of Healing exhibition challenges that idea as healing can be messy, nonlinear, unfinished, and deeply personal." Photography is named among the accepted mediums alongside painting, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media, fiber and ceramics. Each artist may enter up to three works completed in the past three years, original and not previously shown at ALNB, and must write a statement of no more than 100 words explaining how the work answers the exhibition's question; that statement is displayed in the gallery. Juror is Tyler Booth, CEO and President of InterCommunity Health Center, and jurying is hybrid — work is selected online from photographs, with prize winners chosen in person after drop-off. Awards are $200 first place, $100 second and $75 third. Entry is $25 for the first work and $15 for each subsequent work, or $15 and $10 for ALNB members. Registration runs 23 October to 11 December 2026 and notifications go out 20 December 2026. Work may not exceed 72 inches on any unframed side; 2D work must be wired or fitted with D-rings, and images must be unsigned JPEGs under 4 MB in sRGB for anonymous online jurying. AI-generated imagery is not acceptable, and AI-assisted work must be disclosed at submission. Open to artists aged 18 and over. — Deadline: December 11, 2026. Fee: $25 first entry, $15 after (members $15/$10). Prize: $200 / $100 / $75 + exhibition.

item.title: FoMe 2026 International Open Call — INTUITION · FoMe (Fotografía Mexicana)
item.description: First international open call from FoMe (Fotografía Mexicana), a new Mexican photography platform whose inaugural fair runs during Mexico City Art Week, 3–7 February 2027. The theme is INTUITION, "inviting photographers to explore its role as a subject or as part of their creative process", and all photographic genres and approaches are welcome. Fifty artists are selected to exhibit one photograph each, with printing and mounting fully funded by FoMe; all works are offered for sale, artists retain copyright, and the artist receives 65% of the sale price excluding indirect taxes. The six-member jury — Pablo Ortiz Monasterio, Yvonne Venegas, Santiago Arau Pontones, Ana Hop, Manolo Márquez and Greta Rico — votes in two rounds, first choosing the fifty photographs for the Official Selection, then selecting the FoMe Prize winner from among them. The FoMe Prize is MXN 120,000 (approximately US$6,000 less applicable taxes) and does not involve acquiring the work or transferring copyright; there is also a Photographers' Prize chosen by vote of the exhibiting artists. Results are announced on 13 December 2026, selected artists confirm and return their final files by 15 December 2026, and the FoMe Prize winner is announced on 7 February 2027. Entry is free: submit one standalone photograph or two to three images from the same project, plus a single PDF containing a portfolio with artist statement and a CV, and a description of up to 250 words relating the proposal to INTUITION. Selected artists supply a 300 dpi TIFF or JPG identical to the file the jury assessed. The call is open to photographers over 18 of any nationality who are the sole authors of their images and who are not represented by a gallery in Mexico at the time of entry; entry is individual, and collective or co-authored works are not eligible. AI-generated or AI-modified images are not eligible, nor are photographs already commercialised or part of an existing commercial edition, or works subject to third-party representation, exclusivity or sales agreements. Unsold work must be collected within 24 hours of the fair closing. The fair also presents a tribute exhibition to Manuel Álvarez Bravo in collaboration with Casa MAB. — Deadline: December 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: MXN 120,000 (~US$6,000) + exhibition with production paid.

item.title: London Artist Showcase — January 2027 · Arrival Gallery
item.description:
Arrival Gallery runs three-day group shows in a rotating list of cities, and this call is for its London show at 56 Dawes Road, Fulham, from 15 to 17 January 2027. It has an open theme and is open to all visual media, including fine-art, documentary, portrait, street and experimental photography; AI-assisted work is on its list of accepted mediums.
Submitting is free, but the show is paid for by the artists who are selected. The London page sells three routes: a Digital Showcase from £65, where the work is shown on screens without shipping anything; a Physical Showcase from £165, with the work hung in the space; and a limited Featured place with extra promotion, whose price is not published. When read on 2 November the page listed 22 digital, 22 physical and 3 featured places as available in the current batch. The exact fee, format and timeline are sent after selection, before the artist confirms a place. Physical work has to be delivered or shipped by the artist.
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup. The application link asks for a name and email address, with a marketing-email consent box and a choice of medium, and sends a Typeform link to that address. Selected artists get a place in the show, preparation guidance and promotion through Arrival's channels, and may be considered for its other cities. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free (£65+ digital, £165+ physical if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Shadow Work · Visionary Art Collective
item.description: A curated virtual exhibition with an accompanying print catalog, selected by Etta Harshaw for Visionary Art Collective, the Brooklyn-based art and career-development organisation behind New Visionary magazine, the New Visionary Podcast and a programme of virtual and in-person shows. The collective takes submissions from artists at every career stage and across all mediums, photography included, and its exhibition calls have run as virtual shows paired with a printed catalog. Submissions are handled on the organisation's Submittable page, which gives the title, the curator and the closing time and nothing more: the call closes at midnight Eastern between December 6 and 7, 2026, and the entry form itself sits behind a Submittable account, so the image count and any submission fee could not be read. The same Submittable page shows a $25 price beside the organisation's concurrent Artist Spotlight form and no price beside this one, while the organisation's two 2026 exhibition calls each charged $25 to $35 on a tiered scale, so treat the cost as unconfirmed rather than free until the form is opened. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Virtual exhibition + print catalog.

item.title: F-Stop Magazine Issue #141 — Abstraction 2027
item.description: Abstraction in photography, for the February/March 2027 issue of F-Stop Magazine, the online photography magazine that has published themed issues since 2003. Issue #141 asks for up to 12 photographs; a project statement is optional for themed issues (it is required only for Portfolio issues). One submission per person per issue, entry is free and there is no payment for images that are included. Submissions go by email, with images at 1200 px on the longest edge, no borders or watermarks, and titles listed as text in the email body. Selected work is published on the magazine's site and stays in the archive indefinitely — F-Stop does not unpublish past issues. Publication is expected around February 1, 2027. — Deadline: January 8, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Juried Theme Gallery: The Natural World · Arizona Photography Alliance
item.description: The third Juried Theme Gallery call of 2026 from the Arizona Photography Alliance, a Tempe-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit running the programme since 2024. The theme is The Natural World: Earth, Wind, Fire and Water as primordial forces that are “neither simply benevolent nor destructive” — fire that warms and consumes, water that sustains and floods, wind that carries seeds and gathers into a gale. Juror Richard Laugharn, an artist working on the natural and cultural histories of the Sonoran Desert Borderlands with an MFA in photography from Arizona State University and work in the Nelson-Atkins Museum and the Center for Creative Photography, picks one first-place winner for a $100 cash award plus two honorable mentions featured on the alliance's website and social channels. Every entrant is represented in the online exhibition, which opens 1 December 2026 — the juror selects one image from each submission. Submit up to three images, no larger than 2 MB and 1,500 pixels on the long side; all photographic media are welcome, analog, digital or alternative process, and AI photography is not accepted. All rights stay with the photographer, entrants may offer their selected image for sale and handle any sale themselves, and AZPA board members may not submit. Entry is open to members and non-members, with the lower rate for members; there are no refunds once entered. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $25 members, $50 non-members. Prize: $100 + online exhibition.

item.title: Ucross Foundation Fall 2027 Residency
item.description: Two- to six-week residency on the Ucross Foundation's 20,000-acre working ranch in northeastern Wyoming, for the Fall 2027 session running from the first Monday in August to the first Friday in December. Residents receive a private studio, living accommodations, lunches delivered to the studio and group dinners prepared Monday to Friday by a professional chef, weekly housekeeping, linens and wireless internet; accepted artists are given a $1,500 stipend check at orientation on the second day of the residency, and provide their own materials and travel. Around 115 artists are hosted each year with up to ten in residence at a time, typically four writers, four visual artists and two composers. Open worldwide to visual artists (photography included), writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary and performance artists, and to collaborative teams of up to three; applicants must show professional standing, both mature and emerging artists of promise are welcome, and the organiser does not accept applications from students at any level. Residents are chosen by a rotating panel of arts and humanities professionals, with notification about sixteen weeks after the call closes. The $40 application fee is non-refundable and never waived; accepted residents also pay a $50 refundable deposit. Artists may return after three years have elapsed since a previous Ucross residency. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $40. Prize: Residency + $1,500 stipend.

item.title: Ucross Fellowship for Native American Artists — Fall 2027
item.description: Free-to-apply four-week fellowship residency at the Ucross Foundation's 20,000-acre ranch in northeastern Wyoming for contemporary Native American visual artists, writers and performers, in the Fall 2027 session running August through early December. Fellows receive uninterrupted time, a private studio, living accommodations, meals prepared by the foundation's professional chef and a stipend, plus an award of $2,000 and the chance to present work publicly — for visual artists typically a featured exhibition in the Ucross Art Gallery, for others a reading or a performance. The fellowship began in 2018 for Native American visual artists with a grant from The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, was extended to writers in 2020 with National Endowment for the Arts funding and to performers with further NEA funding in 2024. Typically only two recipients are selected per discipline each year, and every applicant has the option of also being considered for a standard Ucross residency. There is no application fee. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,000 + exhibition.

item.title: 5X7 Photobook Vol. 3 · Artsin Square
item.description: Open call for the third volume of 5×7 Photobook, the print photobook series from Artsin Square, an independent, artist-run, ad-free international platform that has published magazines, artist books and photobooks since 2019. Vol. 3 is guest-curated by Below Grand Gallery, described by the organiser as a New York-based gallery and curatorial collective on the Lower East Side, artist-led and community-focused. There is no set theme: any genre of photography, any style and any ratio or size, and previously published work is accepted. Selected artists receive a two-page spread in the printed photobook, an online blog feature, a dedicated social media post, a complimentary digital edition and the chance to review and edit their spread before printing; the book is sold online with worldwide shipping and distributed to selected bookstores and galleries. The organiser states that artists keep full ownership and copyright of their images, with permission limited to printing and distributing them in the book and extending to no other use. Submit up to 10 photographs (ideally 300 dpi JPEG under 10 MB) with an optional bio and statement of up to 400 words. The entry form prices 3 images at $25, 5 at $30 and 10 at $40, and offers a separate optional $20 online-interview add-on (non-refundable, featured only if selected). Open to visual artists aged 18 and over from any country, and to organisations submitting on artists' behalf. Notification of selection 20 November 2026. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $25 for 3 images, $30 for 5, $40 for 10. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Not Too Much off the Top: Barbershops and Salons as Gathering Spaces · Arts Council of Fayetteville/Cumberland County
item.description: The Arts Council of Fayetteville/Cumberland County fills its Arts Center Gallery from 22 January to 28 February 2027 with a free-to-enter national exhibition about the Black barbershop and salon — "a haven for the Black community", in curator Karrington Gardner's words, and "not only a space for personal care and maintenance, but also a place for community organizing, and jovial yet critical conversations." The call asks for "a more introspective investigation of this institution" and welcomes "all conversations surrounding the barbershop and salon". Gardner's own statement is a photographic brief in all but name: the faint humming of the clippers, the radio in the background, the overlapping conversations running between the barbershop at the front and the salon at the back, the barber and the hairdresser who know exactly how you like your hair. He names his references — Kerry James Marshall's De Style (1993) and School of Beauty, School of Culture (2012), and Devin Shimoyama's Mighty Mighty: The Barbershop Project (2019), which "challenges the heteronormativity in the Black barbershop and highlights the often-isolating experience of being a LGBTQ+ person in the space" — so the show is already set up for work that complicates the subject rather than only celebrating it. Documentary portraiture, interiors, found and family archive, hand-worked prints: 2D and 3D work in any medium is accepted, and the only physical constraints are a wire backing for anything hung (the gallery uses a walker hanging system) and that the work must fit through a standard door frame. Entry is free, an artist may submit up to three works, and each submission carries one to five images with the title, media, dimensions, year, price or value and a short description of how the work relates to the theme, plus an artist biography and statement. Five cash awards are given: $500 first prize, $300 second, $200 third and two $100 honorable mentions. The jury is a barber and two painters — Tabari Boykin, Amiah Jones and Marquie Walker — alongside Gardner, who co-curated the Say It Loud exhibition and curated the 2026 NC Folk Festival. Entrants must be 18 or older, and the call is addressed to "Black artists of all identities in the diaspora". Acceptances go out 6 January 2027, with a shipping and drop-off window of 7 to 19 January and the opening on 22 January. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 first prize, $300 second, $200 third, 2 × $100 honorable mention + Exhibition.

item.title: Hispanic Culture Review Literary & Photography Contest 2026–2027
item.description: Hispanic Culture Review is George Mason University's bilingual literary and arts journal, and its 2026–2027 contest has a photography and visual arts category of its own, judged and awarded separately from the writing categories. The theme is "Lo que nos une" / "What Unites Us", and the editors frame it against the present moment: "In a world that often emphasizes what separates us, this edition seeks to celebrate the bridges that connect us through empathy and creativity." They quote Eduardo Galeano — "I hope that we can have the courage to be alone and the bravery to take the risk of being together" — and ask applicants three questions: what unity means to them, what shared experiences and values bring people closer, and how we can celebrate difference while building what unites us. Entry is free. A photographer may send up to six works, each submitted separately, as JPEGs at 300 PPI, and the work must be unpublished — not previously published and not under consideration anywhere else, literary blogs included. One work is awarded in each of the three categories (photography and visual arts; poetry; narrative, essay and academic research): the winner receives $100 and a certificate of recognition, and selected works are published in both the print and the digital (Issuu) editions of the magazine. Submissions are accepted in English or Spanish. There are no age or nationality restrictions, with one stated exception — the journal cannot accept entrants whose fiscal residence is in a country under United States sanctions, because it could not deliver the prize money. The general deadline is Sunday 31 January 2027; George Mason students have their own form with an extension to Sunday 14 February 2027. Prizes are issued in spring 2027. CAUTION on the route, not the call: the journal's own site is the organiser's only domain but it does not carry this contest — its newest post is an “Under Construction/Bajo construcción” notice dated 21 November 2024 that still points readers at the 2025–2026 edition, and its “Latest Issue” panel still reads “2020-2021 Edition.” The live 2026–2027 call is on the journal's Submittable, which its own “Submit Here” link goes to; use the submission link on this page rather than hunting for the call on the website. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $100 + Publication.

item.title: Photo Journalism Prize 2027
item.description: The 2027 edition of the Photojournalism Prize opened for submissions on 26 October 2026 and closes 30 April 2027. PJP is an international award for editorial and documentary photography founded by Hossein Farmani — the publisher behind the Lucie Awards and the International Photography Awards — and it states its purpose in political terms: "At a time when media bias and misinformation threaten public trust, we celebrate the photographers who bring clarity, courage, and integrity to urgent stories of our time." It explicitly opens the field beyond staff press work, saying it exists to recognise "a new era of grassroots storytelling — where independent voices, community reporters, and citizen journalists contribute to the global record". NEW THIS CYCLE: a €5,000 James Nachtwey Prize whose winner Nachtwey selects personally, on top of a €5,000 first prize for the "best overall story with most impact", €3,000 second (jury selection) and €1,000 third (public choice), plus category winners — €14,000 in cash across the four named prizes. Twelve categories: Arts & Culture, Conflict, Daily Life, Documentary, Environment, Human Interest, Human Rights, News, Politics, Portraits, Science & Technology and Sports. An entry is 1 to 10 photographs, and entries of two or more "should form a cohesive story or concept" judged as a series; files are JPG/RGB, up to 4 MB, 1000px minimum on the short side and 2000px maximum on the long side. Work must have been made within the past year. Judging is blind — "photographer identities remain anonymous" — against news value, human interest, visual storytelling, photographic quality, editing and overall reporting, by a jury that includes James Nachtwey, Steve McCurry, Paolo Pellegrin, Ron Haviv, Alex Pollack of National Geographic and photo editors from The Guardian and Lonely Planet. Entry is €25 professional / €20 amateur, with professionals judged against professionals and students against students, open to anyone 18 or over anywhere in the world. There are no refunds once paid. Winners are announced about six weeks after the close, at the Ostuni Foto Festival in Italy; the organiser's FAQ still carries the 2026 cycle's announcement dates, so treat mid-June 2027 as approximate until PJP publishes the 2027 date. — Deadline: April 30, 2027. Fee: €20–€25. Prize: €5,000 / €5,000 / €3,000 / €1,000.

item.title: Source Graduate Photography Online 2027 — BA
item.description: Source's annual graduate showcase, running since 2007, opens its 2027 BA cycle. Open to any BA photography course in the UK or the Republic of Ireland; a year group books a place together (minimum five students) and a lead student uploads everyone's material and makes one payment. Each participating student gets their own permanent page on the Source website carrying up to eight images, a 120-word artist statement and a link to their own site — the magazine's point being that the work stays visible long after degree-show week, in front of a readership it describes as curators, picture editors and publishers. Three selectors then review everything submitted and pick favourites, which are published on the site and in the printed Graduate Photography Online supplement. The 2027 BA selectors are Jess Baxter, Assistant Curator of International Art at Tate Modern; Jean-Christophe Godet, founder and artistic director of the Guernsey Photography Festival; and Isaac Huxtable, Assistant Curator of Photography at the V&A. Submission is eight jpegs at 72 DPI, 1024px on the longest edge, sRGB — fewer than eight is allowed, moving image is not accepted, and each student picks one of six categories (Documentary/Photojournalism, Commercial/Fashion, Landscape, Portraiture, Staged/Constructed, Urban/Suburban Landscape). If the work is made for a gallery, Source recommends one of the eight be an installation shot. The £33 (UK) / €38 (Ireland) per-student fee includes a free one-year digital subscription to Source, which the magazine values at £44.99. The MA/MFA phase of the same programme has a separate, later deadline of 7 August 2027. — Deadline: May 11, 2027. Fee: £33 / €38. Prize: Online exhibition + publication.
