item.title: THE THIRD SPACE: CULTURAL HYBRIDITY — November 2026 Open Call · Thirdplat
item.description: Thirdplat's free monthly open call for November 2026 asks what happens when cultures with their own histories, identities and forms of expression meet through globalisation. The platform's own framing: "A local craft may adopt digital tools, folk music may enter an electronic composition, different languages may share a single poem, or traditional imagery may find a new life in global fashion and film. These encounters can produce connection, tension, resistance and unexpected new forms." It wants work that "begin[s] with specific cultural materials, symbols, customs, languages or techniques and show[s] what happens when they come into contact", and it poses the hard question directly: "When does exchange become appropriation, and when does a hybrid form develop a voice of its own?" Photography is named outright among the welcomed forms — "Whether manifested as moving image, photography, writing, craft, sound, performance or cross-disciplinary work, Thirdplat welcomes original and respectful creations that explore cultural fusion, conflict, transformation and the new identities formed in between." This is publication rather than competition: Thirdplat is an independent online platform that publishes accepted work directly into a permanent public archive, and its Terms of Use state plainly that "Submission is free" and that "No payment, prize, commission or commercial agreement is created by submitting". Six works are already published under this theme. Submitting runs through a Thirdplat account and the platform's Terms of Use set the only entry bar: “You must be at least 18 years old to create an account or submit work through Thirdplat.” Submissions close 30 November 2026; the platform's December theme (REFLECTION: AI AND US, closing 31 December 2026) and January 2027 theme (Counter-Memory) are open alongside it. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Emerging Artist Award 2027 · Pence Gallery
item.description: The Pence Gallery in Davis gives one emerging California artist $4,000 to push new work in a significant direction, plus a solo exhibit and an artist talk at the gallery from 14 January to 27 February 2028. Applicants may work in any medium except video or sound, so photography is eligible, and the gallery asks for a resume with exhibition history and education, an artist statement and 10 to 15 digital images of current work. 'Emerging' is the gallery's own definition — early in an art career, with limited exhibiting experience but not an extensive solo exhibition history — and the submitted work must be high calibre, original and made within the past five years. Applicants must live in California at the time of applying and be 18 or over. The award is sponsored by Rosa Marquez and Yatish Mishra, and the winner is announced by 30 April 2027. One caution on dates: the gallery's own Call for Artists page does not carry this cycle at all — the string '2027' appears nowhere on it, its Emerging Artist Award block still shows last cycle's extended deadline of 12 April 2026, and every neighbouring call there reads 'APPLICATION IS CLOSED' — so this listing points at the gallery's own CaFÉ record, which states 5 April 2027 at 9pm PST twice and dates the resulting exhibition to 2028. The record's structured close instant is end of day Pacific while its prose says 9pm, so treat 9pm PST on 5 April 2027 as the cutoff and confirm with the gallery if you are close to the wire. — Deadline: April 5, 2027. Fee: $40 ($35 Pence members). Prize: $4,000 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: No Place Like... · Art Center Sarasota
item.description: Art Center Sarasota's Atrium Gallery juried show for spring 2027 asks artists to explore ideas of home, belonging and place in an ever-shifting world: domestic spaces, migration, memory, landscape, community or imagined environments, read personally, culturally or conceptually, and reflecting on how place shapes identity, experience and connection. Submissions are welcome in all media, with photography named explicitly alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, digital arts, sculpture and video; work made with generative AI tools is not eligible. Editioned photographic prints are allowed if labelled as prints and numbered, and work must be original, finished within the last three years and not previously shown at the Art Center. The juror is Greg Rumph, Assistant Principal at Booker High School in Sarasota, where he runs the Visual and Performing Arts programme; he holds a BFA in Illustration from Ringling College and two master's degrees from the University of South Florida, and two of his own paintings are in the permanent collection of the National Civil Rights Museum in Memphis. Jurying is blind — the juror sees everything except the artist's name and the price — and the awards are chosen in person once the show is hung: $500 for first place, $300 for second, $200 for third, plus two merit awards and four honourable mentions. Up to three works may be entered; 2D work may not exceed 72 by 65 inches after framing, 3D work 60 by 36 by 36 inches. Note that the Art Center's own website prints the deadline as 'Sunday, February 7, 2026' while its submission portal gives 'Sunday, February 7, 2027' — 7 February 2027 is the Sunday, the portal's own clock closes the form then, and the show runs in 2027, so the year on the website is a typo. All work must be offered for sale, with no NFS or price-on-request, and the artist receives 60% of the selling price as a member or 50% as a non-member. Artists are notified by 17 February 2027, work is received in person on 2 and 3 March or must arrive by post between 1 and 3 March, and the exhibition runs 11 March to 17 April 2027 with an opening reception on 11 March. — Deadline: February 7, 2027. Fee: $40 for 1 work, $65 for 3 ($30–$45 members, $10–$35 students). Prize: $500 / $300 / $200 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Woman Artist Award — 7th Edition · Arts to Hearts Project
item.description: The seventh edition of Arts to Hearts Project's annual prize for women artists, open worldwide with no set theme: any subject, any style, and every medium the organisers list by name - painting, drawing, illustration, sculpture, printmaking, photography, collage, ceramics, textiles, fiber art, installation, performance, digital art, mixed media and interdisciplinary practice. Selected artists are published in Women Artists on the Rise - 5th Edition, the hardcover coffee-table book the Award feeds; the Award and the book are two halves of one initiative, which is why the editions are numbered differently. The Main Prize Winner takes US$500, an engraved glass trophy in a velvet case with a certificate, a full-length interview in the book, an extensive interview on the Arts to Hearts website with social promotion to an audience of 200,000+, a one-year portfolio feature in the Women in Arts Network (valued at US$196) and a year of the Arts to Hearts print and digital magazine. The two runners-up receive trophies, certificates, website interviews, a Women in Arts Network feature (twelve months and six months respectively) and magazine subscriptions; the top three are also offered mentorship calls with art professionals and a Fiber Art Now subscription. Open to women artists 18 and over anywhere in the world, emerging and mid-career, with original work only. Entry is by package and non-refundable: the FAQ prices one artwork at $21, three at $35, five at $47, ten at $62 and twenty at $100, with images in high-resolution JPG or PNG - though the entry form itself prices the single-artwork rung at $12, so the cheapest package carries two figures on the organiser’s own surfaces. A separate $27 add-on buys a customised artist interview on the Arts to Hearts website; it is optional, published only if you are selected, and not refundable. Past sponsors and collaborators include Alicia Puig of PxP Contemporary, Ekaterina Popova of Create! Magazine, Ashley Longshore, Marina Granger of The Artist Advisory, gallerist Liz Lidgett and Fiber Art Now; the organisers put past prize support across all editions at more than US$10,000. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 for 1–20 artworks ($12 first rung on the entry form). Prize: $500 + trophy + publication.

item.title: Spring 2027 SFW Resident Artist Program — SERVICE · Kent Cultural Alliance
item.description: A six-week live-in, work-in residency in Chestertown, Maryland on the theme of SERVICE — work made to serve the needs of the communities it is made for. The session runs March 14 to April 24, 2027, in partnership with For All Seasons, the Kent County Food Pantry and Sumner Hall; three artists are selected. Each receives a $7,500 stipend, travel reimbursement up to $1,000 and studio and gallery expense reimbursement up to $1,500, with accommodation at the Vincent & Leslie Prince Raimond Cultural Center, a 1799 building the National Park Service has selected as an escape site on its Network to Freedom. Community engagement is the cornerstone: residents are embedded with a local partner organisation for the first week, then have five weeks to make finished or substantially finished work, alongside one or two workshops with a local social-service agency or school, an open studio Saturday and two or three evening presentations. Work is exhibited in KCA's 1,000 sq ft gallery after an opening reception on the final Friday of the session; artists may sell, and KCA takes no commission and does not broker. There is no fee to apply, but the application is more than a form: two required narrative statements of 500 words or less — one on the link between your work and community engagement, one on your connection to the theme of SERVICE — plus up to 4 images of current work and links to a website and/or social media. Photography is not named as a category, but the application form states that 'all disciplines of artistry are encouraged including visual art, creative writing, music, fashion, dance, etc.' — an open list. Eligibility is post-degree career artists based in the USA; international artists only with a current visa permitting legal work in the USA (no tourist visas); no current degree candidates. The residency cannot accommodate children, families or pets; the building is fully accessible and includes an ADA-compliant bedroom. Deadline is December 1, 2026 at 5:00 pm EST — a 5 pm cutoff, not midnight. A second open call for the Fall 2027 session is expected. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $7,500 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Industry, Labor, and Community AIR 2027 · WVU Libraries
item.description: WVU Libraries' Art in the Libraries Program invites artists to work with the Industry, Labor, and Community collections at the West Virginia & Regional History Center — union records, company-town archives, oral histories and grassroots community papers — and make new work from them. The 2027 cycle's theme is Common Threads: Industry, Labor & Community. Photography is explicitly in the accepted media list, and the organiser's own examples name a 'Photographic Series' responding to archival images. The award is $1,000 for materials paid on signing, up to $3,500 in reimbursement for transportation, lodging and per diem, and a $1,000 honorarium on completion. The residency is a 5–7 day stay in Morgantown in March or April 2027, including at least two full days in the WVRHC archives, followed by a public programme and exhibition launch at the WVU Downtown Library in April 2027 and a 20-minute community presentation. Ownership of the finished work remains entirely with the artist. Juried by the WVU Art in the Libraries Committee with WVRHC archivists and guest juror Rachel Johnson of the Morgantown Arts Council. Proposals that highlight underrepresented narratives, elevate local working-class history or explore the human impact of regional industry are given strong consideration, and WVU alumni and underrepresented artists are especially encouraged. Note that the page states its geography twice and differently: the programme description says 'open to all U.S. and Canadian-based artists' while the Application Process block, which governs, says 'based in the United States'. Apply by emailing a single combined PDF (abstract, statement of interest, timeline and budget, artist statement, 2-page CV, 5–10 images or web links) to the curator. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 honorarium + Exhibition.

item.title: Fall 2027 - Spring 2028 Solo Exhibitions · SRO Photo Gallery, Texas Tech University
item.description: SRO Photo Gallery is a graduate-student-run exhibition space inside the Digital and Narrative Arts program at the Texas Tech University School of Art, and its annual open call programmes a whole academic year: six to eight solo exhibitions of still photographic work plus four solo moving-image exhibitions, shown between August 2027 and May 2028. A solo slot, not a group hang. Submission is free and goes by email, with no platform in between. Two physical constraints are worth reading before you apply, because they shape what can be shown: prints are displayed unframed — matted, loose, or mounted on thin backing — inside eight glass display cases measuring 30 x 72 x 1 inches each, and moving image work is shown on four wall-mounted monitors side by side (.MOV, .MPG and MPEG-4 only), so video applicants are asked for four 2-5 minute teasers from the same project. Still-image applicants send a PDF slideshow of 20 images at 2000 pixels on the long edge, with title, medium, dimensions and year, plus a bio or CV and an artist or project statement carrying full contact details. Portfolios are reviewed by a committee of Digital & Narrative Arts faculty and students together with the Landmark Arts staff; the gallery asks for lens-based work in any style, technique or aesthetic approach, and says consistency in the work, as well as creative vision, is what weighs in the selection process. The deadline is published as a bare date with no time of day and no timezone on either of the two pages that carry it, and 28 March 2027 falls on a Sunday, so treat the Friday before as the working cutoff. Selected artists are announced in early May 2027 and are reproduced in a full-colour brochure published annually and distributed locally and nationally. The call carries no entry fee and no cash prize. — Deadline: March 28, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition + printed brochure.

item.title: PhotoNOLA PhotoBOOK Prize 2026 · New Orleans Photo Alliance
item.description: The New Orleans Photo Alliance's third annual photobook prize, decided around the PhotoNOLA PhotoBOOK Fair at the historic Patrick F. Taylor Library inside the Ogden Museum of Southern Art — Saturday 5 December 2026, 11am–4pm, inside the 21st PhotoNOLA festival (2–6 December). Open to any artist who has published a photobook in the past five years, with self-published titles explicitly welcomed and encouraged. Two cautions, both measured on the page itself: it gives the eligibility window twice and the two disagree — the guidelines say December 2021 to December 2026, while the entry form's own publication-date field still says "Book must be published between December 2020 and December 2025", which is last year's wording carried over. And its single deadline sentence reads "Sunday, November 13th, 11:59pm" with no year, but 13 November 2026 is a Friday; we store the earlier of the two readings, so treat Friday the 13th as the cutoff and do not count on the 15th. The Grand Prize is $500 plus a Silver NOPA membership; an Award of Excellence and a Louisiana Award of Excellence — the latter reserved for a Louisiana resident, who is also considered for all three prizes — each carry a Silver membership. All three winners are offered the chance to be included at the 2026 Photobook Prize table at the 2027 PhotoNOLA PhotoWALK and Photobook Fair; the page words that as an opportunity, not a guarantee. You enter the book itself through the form on PhotoNOLA's own page: a PDF of the whole volume and a description of up to 600 words are required, a photograph of the book is optional. No juror is named. — Deadline: November 13, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $500 + NOPA membership + fair table.

item.title: In The Abstract 2027 — Virtual Exhibition · San Fernando Valley Arts & Cultural Center
item.description: SFVACC's annual abstract-art open call, in its virtual edition: a juried online exhibition running 24 February to 30 April 2027. The geography is worth reading twice before paying: the prospectus body says the show "is open to all artists" and the CaFE record's location bucket reads International, but the binding Eligibility Criteria field on the same page narrows it — "In The Abstract a Virtual Exhibition is open to all artists residing in North America." Outside the US, Canada or Mexico, ask SFVACC before entering. The brief is the broad one — "Abstract art uses shapes, forms, color, line and texture as opposed to representing an accurate depiction of visual reality" — and the organiser says it "seeks artists who can provide a well-rounded range of 2D and 3D abstract art." Photographers are in scope on the prospectus's own terms: up to six original works per artist, submitted as JPEGs, "in all media except video." Juror Genie Davis, a writer, art curator and the owner of Diversions Fine Arts Gallery in Manhattan Beach, selects an $800 Best of Show (plus a listing on SFVACC's Best of Show page), $400 first place, $300 second place and up to four Honorable Mentions. Entry is $40 for the first work with up to five more at $5 each, and SFVACC is running an early-bird code (SaveVirtual) that takes $10 off until 30 November 2026. The sales terms are unusually clean for an online show: buyers contact the artist directly through the exhibition page, SFVACC takes no commission at all, and prices are fixed at the figure given at submission. Three conditions to read first: work made under an instructor's direct supervision is not eligible, a submitted work cannot be substituted or withdrawn, and work previously shown in any SFVACC exhibit should not be entered. Accepted work stays online until the exhibition closes. Entries close 24 January 2027 at 11:59pm PST, with acceptances emailed by 31 January. — Deadline: January 24, 2027. Fee: $40 ($30 with early-bird code until Nov 30), $5 each additional. Prize: $800 / $400 / $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: In The Abstract 2027 — In-Person Exhibition · San Fernando Valley Arts & Cultural Center
item.description: The gallery half of SFVACC's annual abstract open call: a juried show at TAG Gallery, 5458 Wilshire Boulevard in Los Angeles, running 24 February to 19 March 2027. The theme is abstraction broadly understood — "shapes, forms, color, line and texture as opposed to representing an accurate depiction of visual reality" — and the organiser asks for "a well-rounded range of 2D and 3D abstract art." Photography qualifies on the prospectus's own wording — up to six original works per artist, juried from JPEGs — but this edition carries format bars the virtual one does not: "No AI. No Video. No giclee prints.", a 30-inch maximum in every direction including the frame for wall work, 2D work wired and ready to hang, and "Only plexiglass on 2D work. No glass!" If your prints are pigment inkjet, put the giclée line to SFVACC before paying — the organiser does not define the term. Juror Genie Davis, writer, curator and owner of Diversions Fine Arts Gallery in Manhattan Beach, picks an $800 Best of Show plus a listing on SFVACC's Best of Show page, $400 first place, $300 second place and up to four Honorable Mentions, announced at the opening reception. The hard constraint is delivery: artists must hand-deliver and collect the work themselves at TAG Gallery, on set dates in February and March, and no shipped artwork is accepted at all — which in practice limits this edition to artists who can get to Los Angeles. Commercial terms are specific too: all accepted work must be for sale, priced at $250 or more, TAG Gallery takes 35% of any sale and pays the artist 65% about 60 days after the show closes, while SFVACC takes nothing. Work made under an instructor's direct supervision is not eligible, a submitted work cannot be substituted or withdrawn, and work already shown in an SFVACC exhibit should not be entered. Entry is $40 for the first piece and $5 for each of up to five more; entries close 24 January 2027 at 11:59pm PST with acceptances emailed by 31 January. — Deadline: January 24, 2027. Fee: $40 first entry, $5 each additional. Prize: $800 / $400 / $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: E Pluribus: From Many · Latino Arts, Inc.
item.description: Latino Arts marks forty years of programmes rooted in "Cultura y Corazón: Culture and Heart" with a juried exhibition at its Milwaukee gallery, 5 March to 4 June 2027, made with the Milwaukee Institute of Art & Design and the Richard and Ethel Herzfeld Foundation. E Pluribus means "from many," and the show is about how many voices, histories and traditions can sit together while staying distinct: work is invited through personal, cultural, community-based or cross-cultural perspectives on the mix of cultures, practices and lived experiences that shape Hispanic and Latino identities. The call is open to artists from within the Latino/Hispanic community and to artists who are allies of it through their practice, and the organiser is explicit about how that is read — "The process does not ask whether a work is Hispanic or Latino enough." Applicants must be 18 or over and live in Wisconsin, Iowa, Minnesota, Illinois or Michigan. Up to two original works per artist, no collaborations, completed in 2025 or later, nothing that has already won an award in another juried show, and the work must be two-dimensional, within 6ft high by 8ft wide by 2in deep — which photographs satisfy on the organiser's own criterion. "Digital art is welcome, though strictly NO AI generated images will be allowed." Artists choose one of two tracks for both submissions, Emerging or Established, each defined by practice rather than by age, schooling or sales: the Jurors' Choice recognition is $1,000 in the Established track and $800 in the Emerging one. Required with every entry, beyond the images: an artist statement of 100–250 words and a biography of no more than 150 words. One content rule applies to the work itself — it "must not contain explicit language or sexual imagery." Entry is $40 per artwork, so two works cost $80. Selected artists arrange delivery and transport of the work to the Milwaukee gallery themselves, on set dates in late February 2027. Submissions opened 30 October 2026 and close Sunday 10 January 2027 at 11:59pm CST, with selection notices on 20 January. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: $40 per artwork. Prize: $1,000 / $800 + Exhibition.

item.title: Read This · Fine Line Creative Arts Center
item.description: A Kavanagh Gallery show about text in art, at Fine Line Creative Arts Center in the Fox River Valley about an hour west of Chicago, running 27 May to 9 July 2027. The organiser's framing is deliberately wide: "Combining text with imagery has a long history in art that continues to grow. Artists use text in paintings, prints, and other 2-dimensional art forms, as well as carved and stamped into 3-dimensional sculptures, pottery, and glass. Whether the text is with or without literal meaning, hidden within the piece or clearly visible, the work must contain text as part of the composition." That is the only constraint on subject, and the media bar is simply "All media will be accepted" — which makes it an open door for photographers working with signage, letterforms, handwriting, documents or any image that carries words. $800 in prizes will be awarded; the judge is listed as to be determined. Open to any artist 18 or older resident in the United States, up to three pieces for a single non-refundable $35 entry, one entry per artist, with selections made from the submitted images on creativity, quality of artistry and originality. Two required items are easy to miss: an artist statement of no more than 1,000 characters that "must not include the artist’s name", and a sale price on every piece — "Artwork on an application without a sale price will not move to the jury phase." Three practical conditions are worth pricing before entering: the artist pays shipping to and from Fine Line and must include a return label, the artist insures the work in transit (Fine Line deems the insurance value to be 70% of the sale price), and because this is a selling gallery show all accepted work must be for sale with a 30% commission on anything sold — Fine Line handles the sales and sales tax and pays out after the show closes. Applications are due 12 April 2027, jury decisions go out by email on 23 April, and work is delivered and checked in on 22 May 2027. — Deadline: April 12, 2027. Fee: $35/3 works. Prize: $800 in prizes + Exhibition.
